card: Caps the timeout argument in Sock::WaitMany to INT_MAX milliseconds (~24.8 days) to prevent large timeout values from failing select() or overflowing poll(). Setting -rpcclienttimeout=0 (no timeout) currently fails immediately on macOS with 'Could not connect to the server' because bitcoin-cli maps 0 to a 5-year duration, exceeding macOS select()'s 10^8-second limit. The fix applies universally to Sock::WaitMany callers and includes a unit test reproducing the 5-year timeout failure.
changed_since_previous: Dropped the Sock::NO_TIMEOUT constant and changes to bitcoin-cli callers; the PR now simply clamps timeout values directly in Sock::WaitMany.
evidence: PR description: 'bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0 is documented as "no timeout", but on macOS it fails with "Could not connect to the server" since #34342 (it's in v32.0rc1/rc2).'
PR description: 'The new sock_tests/wait_large_timeout test waits with a 5 year timeout on a socket that already has data. It fails on master on macOS and passes with this change.'
problem: Running bitcoin-cli with -rpcclienttimeout=0 (documented as no timeout) fails immediately on macOS and BSD systems with 'Could not connect to the server'. bitcoin-cli converts a zero timeout into a 5-year duration (~1.58 * 10^8 seconds), which causes select() to fail with EINVAL on platforms like macOS that reject timeouts exceeding 10^8 seconds.

risk.why: Incorrect timeout clamping could cause socket operations to return earlier than expected, but INT_MAX milliseconds (~24.8 days) is far beyond normal RPC wait times.

summary: Caps the timeout duration in Sock::WaitMany to INT_MAX milliseconds (~24.8 days). This prevents extremely large timeout values from failing system calls like select() or overflowing poll() parameter types.
